evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never delivered the recognizable version framing time-boxed scope, promise of dependable quote, and wait for explicit yes before proceeding. Jumped directly into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move, and what do you want answers to on this call?' — probing began immediately after availability check.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep gathered property type (two-story house), square footage (4500-4600 sq ft), floor/stairs detail (one flight), additional rooms (3 bedrooms of stuff), access/driveway, special considerations (long bike 15-16 feet, gym equipment, heavy boxes of mats/dumbbells up to 120 lbs), storage details (two 10x25 indoor units, one full/one 3/4 full), and prior mover crew size (two 26-foot trucks + 4-man crew).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided hourly rate ($400/hour with four movers), duration estimate (8–9 hours), and personalized total range ($3,200–$3,600) tied to customer's specific move (two trucks, four movers, gym equipment upstairs, long bike, heavy items). Rep also explicitly stated 'all in' — no trip fees, loading, travel, insurance, taxes all included.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed 'no trip fees or anything that is all in' and listed loading/travel/insurance/taxes included, but did NOT frame the '2.5-hour minimum' / '15-minute-increments' / 'not a guess' commitment language from the script.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' and did not pause for customer reaction to the estimate. Moved directly to 'Alright, did you have any other questions so far?'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Not mentioned at any point in the call.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Not mentioned at any point in the call.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asked 'Alright, did you have any other questions so far?' — a throwaway 'any questions?' not the genuine version 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep said 'Well then I'm gonna go ahead and I will send you a confirmation email as well right now' and 'right now I do have the two trucks reserved for you.' Implicit booking acceptance, but no direct ask like 'Would you like our help with your move?' Customer offered 'why don't we pencil it in for right now' — rep accepted but did not initiate the ask plainly.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed date (Friday Sept 25), sent confirmation email, reserved two trucks. Did NOT confirm full arrival window, specific crew size on day-of, full addresses re-verified, or notes left for crew about customer's concerns (gym equipment placement, long bike, heavy boxes).

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered comprehensive logistics detail across storage unit specs, special items (gym equipment, long bike, weight details), home layout, access, and room-by-room placement — nearly professional-level discovery that surfaced everything needed to scope the move accurately.
coaching_note: Skip the immediate probing and deliver the full Section 1 quid pro quo framing (time-boxed + dependable quote promise + wait for yes) before asking any questions, then circle back to ask Section 2's genuine concerns agenda instead of diving straight into logistics — this creates permission and uncovers what actually matters to the customer before pinning down details.
booking_note: Customer explicitly agreed to pencil in the move for Friday September 25th: 'why don't we pencil it in for right now' and sales rep confirmed 'I do have the two trucks reserved for you'
